title: Empty set
summary: An empty set is a set with no members; existence and uniqueness come from the declared set theory.

context.note: Revision 2 distinguishes the defining property from the axioms used to establish existence and uniqueness.

assumptions.text: The ambient theory proves existence of a memberless set.
Extensionality is available to prove uniqueness.

content.plain: The empty set has no members. Its existence is theory-relative, and extensionality makes it unique when it exists.
content.exact: Empty(E) iff E is a set and ∀x ¬(x∈E). In the declared presentation, empty-set existence gives some E with Empty(E), and extensionality proves ∀E∀F[(Empty(E)∧Empty(F))→E=F].
content.example: The solution set of x²=-1 over the real numbers is empty.
content.caveat: Some set-theory axiom lists derive existence from separation and another existence axiom instead of naming a separate empty-set axiom.

verification.method: QEVA 0.5 protocol audit corrected scope, assumptions, and dependency semantics; no formal proof is claimed.

provenance.creator: QEVA 0.5 mathematical protocol audit
provenance.source_note: Adds the missing extensionality dependency and separates definition, existence, and uniqueness. This is an original QEVA formulation and remains subject to independent review.
